altostratus-cloud.context: A flat, even sheet of cloud with a dim sun disk glowing through it and faint light below. Used in cloud identification guides, weather apps and sky watching lessons.

stratocumulus-cloud.context: Two low layers of lumpy, rounded cloud rolls packed side by side. Used for cloud identification, aviation weather and overcast but dry forecasts.

towering-cumulus.context: A tall cauliflower shaped cumulus cloud with stacked lobes rising from a flat base. Used for convection, afternoon showers and developing storm alerts.

pileus-cloud.context: A rounded cumulus cloud with a thin, smooth cap cloud arched just above its top. Used in cloud guides and to show strong updrafts in growing storms.

roll-cloud.context: A long tube shaped cloud lying low over a flat horizon, with a curl at its end showing it rolls. Used for arcus and volutus clouds, gust fronts and coastal weather.

asperitas-cloud.context: A cloud whose underside hangs in deep rolling waves above a wavy line, like a rough sea seen from below. Used in cloud guides and dramatic sky photography.

kelvin-helmholtz-cloud.context: A row of cloud crests curling over like breaking waves along one cloud layer. Used for wind shear, turbulence and fluid dynamics topics.

fallstreak-hole.context: A cloud layer with a clear oval hole in the middle and wispy streaks of falling ice trailing inside it. Used in cloud guides and unusual sky phenomena lists.

pyrocumulus-cloud.context: A puffy cloud billowing up from a smoke column above a line of flames. Used for wildfire alerts, fire weather and smoke forecasts.

cap-cloud.context: A mountain with a smooth lens shaped cloud sitting on its summit like a hat. Used for mountain weather, hiking forecasts and orographic cloud guides.

banner-cloud.context: A pointed mountain peak with a cloud streaming sideways from its lee side like a flag. Used for mountain weather, high wind warnings and climbing forecasts.

cloud-streets.context: Three rows of small puffy clouds lined up one behind the other and shrinking into the distance. Used for convection, cold air outbreaks and satellite image topics.

cloud-levels-chart.context: A height axis with wispy high cloud at the top, a lumpy mid level cloud in the middle and a flat low layer near the ground. Used to teach cloud types and heights.

forest-mist.context: A row of pointed conifer trees with soft bands of mist drifting above them. Used for misty mornings, damp forests, hiking and nature apps.

valley-fog.context: Two rounded hills under a clear sun with fog lying low beneath them in the valley. Used for radiation fog, morning fog advisories and landscape weather.

sea-fog.context: Two bands of fog drifting over a wavy sea, with a lighthouse half hidden behind them. Used for marine forecasts, coastal fog warnings and shipping.

steam-fog.context: Curling wisps of vapor rising from the calm surface of a lake. Used for steam fog, sea smoke, cold mornings over water and evaporation topics.

hexagonal-plate-snowflake.context: A flat six sided plate of ice with an inner hexagon and ridges running to each corner. Used for snow crystal science, winter themes and cold weather.

column-snowflake.context: A short upright six sided ice column with a hexagon end face, like a tiny prism. Used for snow crystal types and cold cloud science.

hailstone-cross-section.context: A lumpy hailstone cut open to show a growth ring around a small central core. Used for hail science, storm education and severe weather.

diamond-dust.context: A low sun on the horizon with tiny ice glints sparkling in the clear air above it. Used for diamond dust, ice fog and very cold clear days.

lake-effect-snow.context: A cloud band forming over a lake and dropping a snowflake onto the far shore. Used for lake effect snow warnings, snow squalls and regional forecasts.

wind-driven-rain.context: A cloud with rain streaks slanting sharply sideways and a gust of wind beside it. Used for storm warnings, driving rain and wind and rain forecasts.

snow-roller.context: A hollow cylinder of wind rolled snow resting on a flat snowy surface. Used for rare winter phenomena, snow science and wind topics.

sastrugi.context: A snow surface carved by the wind into sharp wavy ridges, with a gust blowing across. Used for polar travel, wind erosion and snow surface topics.

snow-load.context: A house with a heavy mound of snow on its roof and an arrow pressing down inside. Used for roof snow load, building codes, insurance and winter safety.

frost-depth.context: A ground cross section with a snowflake below the surface, a dashed frost line deeper down and an arrow showing the depth. Used for construction, plumbing and gardening in cold climates.

freeze-thaw-cycle.context: Two curved arrows cycling between a snowflake and a water drop. Used for freeze thaw weathering, potholes, road damage and melting topics.

snowpack.context: A slope with stacked layers of snow lying on it and a snowflake above. Used for snowpack reports, avalanche safety, water supply and skiing.

rope-tornado.context: A thin twisting rope of a tornado hanging from a flat cloud base down to the ground. Used for tornado warnings, storm chasing and weakening tornadoes.

multiple-vortex-tornado.context: A wide tornado funnel of stacked lines with smaller spinning vortices at either side of its base. Used for violent tornadoes, severe weather and storm science.

wind-shear.context: A height axis with wind arrows of different lengths and directions at each level. Used for aviation weather, turbulence and storm forecasting.

sea-breeze.context: A coast with the sun over warm land and a curved arrow carrying a breeze in from the sea. Used for coastal weather, onshore winds, sailing and beach forecasts.

foehn-wind.context: A mountain with a rain cloud on one side and a warm dry wind sweeping down the other side toward the sun. Used for foehn and chinook winds, rain shadows and alpine weather.

katabatic-wind.context: Two arrows of cold air flowing downhill along the surface of a glacier slope. Used for katabatic winds, glacier and polar weather and mountain valleys.

trade-winds.context: A globe with its equator line and arrows on both sides blowing in toward it. Used for trade winds, global circulation, sailing routes and geography lessons.

doldrums.context: A sailboat with a slack, sagging sail on flat water under a blazing sun. Used for calm windless weather, the doldrums near the equator and feeling stuck.

thermal-updraft.context: A spiral of rising warm air above the ground with an arrow at the top and a bird circling above it. Used for thermals, gliding, paragliding and convection topics.

atmospheric-river.context: A wide band of moisture sweeping over the ocean waves and hitting a coastal mountain. Used for atmospheric river storms, heavy rain and flood forecasts.

omega-block.context: A jet stream line bulging up into an omega shaped loop around a letter H. Used for blocking highs, heat domes and stuck weather patterns.

cold-wave.context: A snowflake with wavy lines of cold air streaming behind it. Used for cold wave warnings, cold snaps, frost alerts and winter forecasts.

saffir-simpson-scale.context: A hurricane symbol beside five rising bars, one for each storm category. Used for hurricane category ratings, storm warnings and emergency planning.

enhanced-fujita-scale.context: A small tornado funnel beside six rising bars, like a damage rating scale. Used for tornado ratings, damage surveys and severe weather reports.

hook-echo.context: A radar storm echo with a curling hook at its lower corner inside broken radar rings. Used for tornado radar signatures, supercells and storm spotting.

bow-echo.context: A line of storms bent into a lumpy bow, with an arrow pushing out from behind its middle. Used for derechos, squall lines and damaging wind warnings.

sprite-lightning.context: A storm cloud with a jellyfish shaped glow and hanging tendrils flaring above it. Used for red sprites, upper atmosphere lightning and night sky photography.

st-elmos-fire.context: The top of a ship mast and yard with a glowing flame and sparks around its tip. Used for St Elmo's fire, static electricity, sailing lore and storms at sea.

intracloud-lightning.context: Two clouds side by side with a zigzag lightning bolt running between them. Used for cloud to cloud lightning, thunderstorm activity and lightning detection.

fulgurite.context: A lightning bolt striking a sand surface with a branching glassy tube spreading underground. Used for fulgurites, lightning strikes on the ground and geology.

glory-halo.context: An airplane silhouette inside two circular halo rings, as seen on a cloud top below a plane. Used for the glory optical effect, flight photos and sky optics.

circumzenithal-arc.context: An upturned rainbow shaped arc high in the sky above a low sun on the horizon. Used for halo and sky optics guides and ice crystal phenomena.

green-flash.context: A sun half set into a wavy sea with a bright glint bursting from its top edge. Used for the green flash, sunsets and sunrises at sea and sky optics.

lightning-distance.context: A lightning bolt beside a stopwatch with a dashed line below, for counting the seconds to thunder. Used for lightning safety, storm distance and the 30 30 rule.

station-model.context: A weather station plot with a half filled cloud cover circle, a wind barb and short data marks around it. Used for surface weather maps and meteorology lessons.

cloud-cover-okta.context: A circle with three of its four quarters shaded, the symbol for cloud amount in oktas. Used on station plots, aviation reports and cloud cover forecasts.

isotherm.context: Two wavy contour lines of equal temperature beside a thermometer. Used for temperature maps, isotherm charts and climate zones.

high-pressure-ridge.context: A zigzag ridge axis stretching out from a large letter H. Used on weather maps for ridges of high pressure and fair weather.

low-pressure-trough.context: A dashed trough axis extending out from a large letter L. Used on weather maps for troughs of low pressure and unsettled weather.

dryline.context: A straight line with open half circles along one side, the dry line symbol on weather maps. Used for severe storm forecasting where dry and moist air meet.

thunderstorm-map-symbol.context: The weather map thunderstorm symbol, an R shaped mark whose leg ends in a lightning arrow. Used on station plots and synoptic charts.

shower-map-symbol.context: A downward pointing triangle with a dot above it, the rain shower symbol on weather maps. Used on station plots and synoptic charts.

skew-t-chart.context: A chart with slanted grid lines and two jagged profile curves side by side. Used for skew T diagrams, weather balloon soundings and storm forecasting.

meteogram.context: Three stacked mini charts showing a temperature line, wind barbs and rain bars over time. Used for point forecasts, weather apps and forecast charts.

lapse-rate.context: A height axis with a line slanting toward colder as it rises above a mountain outline. Used for lapse rates, temperature falling with altitude and mountain weather.

spaghetti-plot.context: A bundle of forecast lines starting at one point and spreading apart to the right. Used for ensemble forecasts, storm tracks and forecast uncertainty.

climate-projection.context: A line chart that becomes a widening fan of possible futures after a dashed now line. Used for climate scenarios, projections and uncertainty ranges.

climograph.context: A row of monthly rainfall bars with a curved temperature line running over them. Used for climate graphs, geography lessons and travel climate info.

keeling-curve.context: A graph with a sawtooth line steadily climbing from lower left to upper right. Used for rising carbon dioxide levels, greenhouse gases and climate change.

temperature-distribution-shift.context: Two overlapping bell curves with the second shifted to the right and an arrow above. Used to show warming shifting temperature ranges and more hot extremes.

temperature-record.context: A thermometer reading at its very top beside a prize medal on a ribbon. Used for record high temperatures, hottest days and heat records.

extreme-weather.context: A storm cloud with a lightning bolt, a flame and a water drop clustered beneath it. Used for extreme weather, natural hazards, climate risk and disaster planning.

el-nino.context: An ocean wave under a hot sun with a long arrow pushing warm water east. Used for El Nino, ENSO forecasts, warm ocean phases and seasonal outlooks.

la-nina.context: An ocean wave under a snowflake with a dashed pool of cold water just below the surface. Used for La Nina, ENSO forecasts, cool ocean phases and seasonal outlooks.

thermohaline-circulation.context: An ocean surface wave above a loop of arrows running along the top, sinking deep and returning. Used for ocean conveyor belt, deep currents and climate science.

ice-thickness.context: A cross section of a frozen lake with an ice layer over water and a ruler measuring it. Used for ice safety, ice fishing, skating and lake ice reports.

polar-vortex.context: A globe seen from above the pole with a wavy ring of cold air circling a snowflake. Used for polar vortex news, arctic outbreaks and severe cold forecasts.
